evals.name: smoke-session-opener
evals.prompt: I just landed in a large repository and need the fastest high-signal first pass before I open any files. Use implicit-token-savings.
evals.expected_output: Starts with a sufficient compact inventory such as ls, tree, or rg --files rather than dumping whole files. The comprehensive environment probe is optional.

assertions.text: Mentions a compact repo inventory command such as ls -1, tree -L 2, or rg --files
Uses known availability or a targeted check when needed rather than requiring the comprehensive probe as a session opener

evals.name: edge-rg-missed-file
evals.prompt: rg returned nothing, but I am certain the string exists somewhere in a hidden or ignored file. What is the cheapest next step?
evals.expected_output: Chooses a scoped hidden/ignore override or --debug to resolve the missing-result hypothesis, without repeating a normal search or forcing an escalation ladder.

assertions.text: Selects appropriate rg hidden/ignore handling or --debug based on the uncertainty, without requiring unnecessary intermediate commands
Avoids jumping straight to full-file dumps or whole-repo reads

evals.name: negative-full-file-request
evals.prompt: The user explicitly asked for the full contents of a short config file and does not want optimization advice. How should the skill behave?
evals.expected_output: The response allows a direct full-file read and does not force tree, rg, or git summaries when the user explicitly wants the literal file contents.

assertions.text: States that a full-file read is acceptable when the file is short and explicitly requested
Does not insist on compact commands when they would block the explicit user request

evals.name: disclosure-git-scope-review
evals.prompt: I want the narrowest command sequence for checking staged scope and recent commit history before committing. Which part of the skill should I read and what commands should I use?
evals.expected_output: The response routes to references/git.md and recommends short git status, staged diff stat, and oneline log commands before full diffs.

assertions.text: Routes the user to references/git.md for compact git workflows
Uses git status --short, git diff --cached --stat, or git log --oneline before wider diffs

evals.name: known-file-needs-whole-context
evals.prompt: Review config/runtime.ts for contradictory defaults and overrides. It is 90 lines long, and all sections affect the result. The path and file size are already confirmed.
evals.expected_output: Reads the known file in full immediately rather than discovering it again or requiring a failed narrow excerpt.

assertions.text: Uses a direct whole-file read to inspect defaults and overrides together
Does not run an inventory, search, comprehensive probe, or arbitrary short excerpt as a prerequisite

evals.name: negative-incidental-runner-mention
evals.prompt: Rewrite this sentence for our release notes: 'We switched from pytest to go test for the new service.' Do not inspect or run anything.
evals.expected_output: Edits the sentence without triggering shell-command optimization just because test runners are mentioned.

assertions.text: Does not run or recommend shell probes, inventories, or test commands for a copy-only request

evals.name: required-gate-not-optional
evals.prompt: Finish the authorized lint cleanup in src/api.py. Relevant ruff autofixes are allowed. The repository requires its complete validation suite before handoff even though it is slow. Do not commit or push.
evals.expected_output: Applies and reviews scoped autofixes without asking again, runs the required gate with failure details visible, and respects the no-commit/no-push boundary.

assertions.text: Does not substitute a narrow test for the required full gate or ask for approval solely because the gate is slow
Preserves errors and failure details and performs no commit or push
